description: DEF CON 33 Blacks in Cybersecurity Village features talks, panels, and workshops highlighting career advancement, diversity, and technical tradecraft. Sessions cover reverse engineering with Ghidra, cyberbiosecurity, AI-driven phishing analysis, DNS threat intelligence, and community initiatives across the global cyber ecosystem.

talks.title: RE for the Rest of Us: An Introduction to Reverse Engineering
talks.teaser: Introduces reverse engineering fundamentals using hands-on Arduino hardware and Ghidra binary analysis demos.
talks.summary:
In this practical workshop from the Blacks in Cybersecurity Village at DEF CON 33, cybersecurity researcher Sydney Johns presents an accessible guide to reverse engineering embedded firmware and compiled software binaries. Opening at 00:00, Sydney demystifies the field, reassuring beginners that reverse engineering does not require a computer science degree or mastery of complex assembly language.

At 06:04, Sydney guides attendees through interpreting microcontroller hardware datasheets to identify pinouts, memory configurations, and communication buses. At 12:00, she demonstrates hardware verification using a digital multimeter in continuity mode to trace circuit connections on target printed circuit boards. Moving to software analysis at 18:01, she contrasts high-level source code, compiled assembly instructions, and raw binary representations.

At 24:06, Sydney uploads firmware to an Arduino test board, showing how to extract binary images and load ELF files into disassembly tools. At 32:00, she demonstrates navigating decompiled functions, inspecting control flow graphs, and searching for hardcoded credentials, providing attendees with a reproducible methodology for foundational hardware reverse engineering. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: From Wake Island to the War Room
talks.teaser: Nykolas Muldrow shares experiences navigating cybersecurity leadership and operations from remote military outposts to national defense missions.
talks.summary:
Nicholas Modro, a cybersecurity solutions architect with the US Air Force and CEO of KAI Solutions Global, shares his career trajectory spanning isolated defense outposts to high-stakes executive operations in the Blacks in Cybersecurity Village [00:06]. Reflecting on his formative posting at Wake Island—a remote, geographically isolated military airfield in the Pacific [03:18]—Modro illustrates how constrained environments foster self-reliance, technical adaptability, and deep operational discipline.

Modro introduces key career and operational principles, beginning with the concept of "controlling your narrative" by achieving comprehensive visibility over internal network environments, infrastructure dependencies, stakeholders, and adversary threat models [06:34]. He emphasizes mental resilience in the face of bureaucratic friction [09:38], breaking complex technical certifications down into manageable modular concepts [16:46], and proactive self-advocacy. Modro counsels emerging practitioners not to wait for invitations to executive decision-making spaces, but rather to "build your own table, bolt it down to the floor, and invite others" [13:12], closing with practical strategies for job interviews including reviewing recorded mock sessions with and without audio to master nonverbal communication [23:33].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.teaser: Provides an unfiltered critique of cybersecurity industry hype, vendor promises, and the necessity of practical foundational security over shiny tools.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses.

talks.title: Petty Proteins: When Molecules Go Rogue and Why Cyberbiosecurity Matters
talks.teaser: Explores how AI-designed proteins and biological vulnerabilities mirror cybersecurity attack vectors, highlighting the emerging field of cyberbiosecurity.
talks.summary:
In this pioneering presentation from the Blacks in Cybersecurity Village at DEF CON 33, a doctoral researcher explores the emerging frontier of cyberbiosecurity, examining the intersection of biological sciences, computational pipelines, and digital security threats. Opening at 00:00, the speaker introduces cyberbiosecurity as the discipline tasked with securing synthetic biology infrastructure, DNA synthesizers, and bioinformatics databases against digital tampering.

At 06:03, the speaker contrasts DNA blueprints and RNA messaging with protein execution, explaining that proteins act as the functional molecular "workers" whose behavior governs cellular processes. At 12:02, the talk examines breakthrough deep learning models—such as AlphaFold and ESMFold—that predict complex 3D protein structures within minutes, drastically accelerating research but also introducing potential algorithmic supply chain risks.

At 18:00, the presenter explores hypothetical threat vectors, including poisoned protein folding models, deceptive synthetic payloads, and automated sequence tampering in shared biological repositories. Concluding at 24:00, the speaker calls for proactive defensive research, responsible disclosure protocols, and cross-disciplinary collaboration between security practitioners and computational biologists to safeguard biological data pipelines. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: The African Cybercrime Economy
talks.teaser: Examines the mechanics of the African cybercrime economy and highlights initiatives like GoLegit Africa that create technical training pathways away from cybercrime.
talks.summary:
Cybersecurity consultant and GoLegit Africa founder Femi Afon delivers an in-depth breakdown of the underground cybercrime ecosystem across Africa, detailing organizational structures, primary threat vectors, and intervention strategies [00:07]. Afon analyzes the specialized division of labor powering illicit operations, explaining how syndicates isolate top financiers and organizers while deploying front-line operators, recruitment brokers, "catchers" who manage money-mule bank transfers, and "connectors" who interface with corrupt law enforcement officers paid to obstruct criminal investigations [05:21, 05:45].

Afon examines prominent attack methodologies originating from regional threat actors, including telco-targeted SIM swapping schemes used to hijack accounts [10:46], sophisticated Business Email Compromise (BEC) and fraudulent investment schemes [17:27], cryptocurrency fraud, hospital ransomware attacks [16:06], and predatory sextortion campaigns targeting foreign teenagers [21:34]. Addressing the socioeconomic drivers behind cybercrime—including acute youth unemployment and limited educational pathways [27:12]—Afon outlines GoLegit Africa's grassroots intervention programs, which engage high school and university students to redirect technical talent into ethical hacking, software development, and remote defensive cybersecurity careers [31:57, 40:09].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: How AI Is Revolutionizing Phishing Attacks & Defenses
talks.teaser: Explores the dual role of artificial intelligence in scaling hyper-targeted phishing campaigns while powering real-time behavioral defenses.
talks.summary:
The AI Arms Race in Phishing Attacks

Artificial intelligence and large language models enable cyber adversaries to automate highly tailored, grammatically flawless spear-phishing campaigns at planetary scale, defeating traditional email reputation filters.

AI-Powered Defensive Filtering and Behavioral Analysis

To counter automated threats, defenders deploy machine learning models that analyze communication context, sender behavioral anomalies, and linguistic stylometry in real time.

Evaluating the Dual-Edged AI Security Landscape

Levone Campbell compares offensive generation techniques against adaptive defensive filtering, providing organizations with actionable strategies to secure human communication channels.

talks.title: Breaking Down Bias in the Cyber Stack
talks.teaser: Identifies subtle systemic biases across technical security controls, organizational policies, and hiring pipelines, offering actionable remediation strategies.
talks.summary:
In this reflective and candid session from the Blacks in Cybersecurity Village at DEF CON 33, the speaker leads an in-depth conversation exploring how conscious and unconscious bias permeates every level of the cybersecurity stack. Opening at 00:00, the session examines how systemic preconceptions distort technical hiring, promotion pipelines, organizational policies, and even defensive threat modeling.

At 08:01, the speaker contrasts legacy corporate stereotypes—such as the traditional corporate image of IT personnel—with the lived realities and personal branding of diverse practitioners across the hacker community. At 16:00, the discussion investigates cognitive biases surrounding technical roles, noting how assumptions regarding neurodiversity and gender frequently mischaracterize project managers, engineers, and security analysts.

Addressing cross-cultural workplace dynamics at 24:00, the speaker examines challenges faced by engineers collaborating across multinational teams and navigating corporate code-switching. Concluding past 48:01, the presenter urges cybersecurity leaders to mentor junior talent, cultivate transparent organizational cultures, and recognize that diverse threat modeling perspectives are essential to identifying enterprise blind spots. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Price of Progress: Ethical Cybersecurity in Tech Communities
talks.teaser: Examines ethical challenges and community responsibilities surrounding technological progress and cybersecurity practices in tech communities.
talks.summary:
Cybersecurity professional Joy Tony examines the intersection of professional security ethics, community impact, and the environmental footprint of large-scale technology infrastructure in the Blacks in Cybersecurity Village [00:05]. Grounding her discussion in the ISC2 Code of Ethics canons—which mandate prioritizing the safety of the commonwealth and public trust above corporate convenience [05:27]—Tony urges security practitioners to broaden their threat models beyond traditional corporate perimeter defenses to account for ecological and public harm.

Tony highlights the astronomical resource consumption of artificial intelligence compute clusters, focusing on the acute depletion of municipal power grids and scarce freshwater aquifers utilized by data center cooling systems [11:04]. She contrasts sustainable industrial designs—such as Boyers' underground data facility utilizing closed-loop geothermal lake water filtration [16:33]—with exploitative urban developments, specifically analyzing Elon Musk's xAI "Colossus" supercomputer facility in Southwest Memphis [22:00]. Tony reviews the local civil rights and environmental backlash, detailing unauthorized gas combustion turbines that spurred NAACP Clean Air Act lawsuits [27:32] and the heavy strain placed on community drinking water aquifers [38:02], calling on technologists to hold their organizations accountable to the communities they inhabit [43:26].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Let's Lose the Shock: Mystery of Linux - A Pain Free Intro
talks.teaser: Demystifies the Linux operating system for beginners through relatable Windows comparisons, core architecture explanations, and command-line tips.
talks.summary:
In this foundational tutorial from the Blacks in Cybersecurity Village at DEF CON 33, seasoned IT practitioner DJ Davis delivers an approachable, hands-on introduction to Linux designed to eliminate terminal intimidation for beginners. Opening at 00:00, DJ shares lessons from his extensive career spanning IBM mainframes to modern Unix environments, demystifying the operating system's architecture and command-line interfaces.

At 11:02, DJ breaks down what Linux is and what it is not, explaining the separation between the Linux kernel, device drivers, userland applications, and desktop graphical environments. At 21:02, he explores system runlevels, process initialization, and the Linux Filesystem Hierarchy Standard (FHS), demonstrating how core directories such as /proc and /sys expose real-time process telemetry and system memory state.

Moving into practical terminal operations at 33:00, DJ details Linux file permissions (read, write, execute), user ownership, and directory traversal. At 42:01, he illustrates command piping and standard input/output redirection to combine small utilities into powerful workflows. He concludes at 55:03 by reviewing Unix heritage from Minix to modern distributions, encouraging attendees to build daily familiarity with Linux to advance their cybersecurity careers. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)
